probe_assessment: The claude-haiku cold read at low effort got the module purpose and almost all API roles right. It misread reconcile_sets as handling predicted rally spans, but the signature and body show only ground-truth rallies and per-set CSV tables, so that is a probe error. The single-pair loop is mechanically clear; asking for its rationale is outside this comprehension-only task. The projection's court-coordinate convention and the imported OTHER_HALF mapping are not fully resolvable from this file alone.

probe_findings.claim: The landing-half classification depends on an imported court-coordinate convention. This file does not establish what projected[1, 0] measures or the units and meaning of NET_COURT_Y.
probe_findings.quote:
projected = point_winner.project_pixels_to_court(np.array([[gt_landing[0]], [gt_landing[1]]]), point_winner.HOMOGRAPHY_RESOLUTION, court_info[fixture.video_id])
            landing_half = Half.TOP if float(projected[1, 0]) < point_winner.NET_COURT_Y else Half.BOT

probe_findings.claim: OTHER_HALF is imported and indexed for a lost verdict, but its valid keys, concrete mapping and data structure are defined only in point_winner. Its opposing-half role is inferable, but not fully verifiable here.

verdicts.claim: The abbreviated _norm_half name does not tell a skim reader that only the exact string "Top" is retained and every other input becomes "Bot", including an unrecognised value.
verdicts.quote:
def _norm_half(side: str) -> str:
    return "Top" if side == "Top" else "Bot"
verdicts.suggested_fix: Rename it to _normalize_court_half and document or validate the non-Top input policy.
verdicts.verifier_note: The original misleading-name premise is wrong because coercing values into Top or Bot is normalisation. The telling correction is that the abbreviated name hides the non-Top coercion and court-half domain term. This merges the naming and style findings; one duplicate was folded in.

verdicts.claim: The tolerance formula uses ungrounded numeric literals for a five-frame baseline at 30 fps, nearest-frame rounding via 0.5 and a one-frame minimum.
verdicts.quote:
def canonical_tolerance(fps: float) -> int:
    return max(1, math.floor(5.0 * fps / 30.0 + 0.5))
verdicts.suggested_fix: Name the baseline and minimum as constants or add a short why-comment explaining the scaling and rounding policy.
verdicts.verifier_note: Merged the magic-number and missing-formula-documentation findings. The raw unclear-name category is corrected to style-house under the rubric; one duplicate was folded in.

verdicts.claim: sm_side is an opaque abbreviation for a frame-to-court-half lookup; the reader must infer that purpose from its right-hand side and later uses.
verdicts.quote: sm_side = {int(frame): _norm_half(str(side)) for frame, side in zip(per_vid["frame_num"], per_vid["player_side"])}
verdicts.suggested_fix: Rename it to side_by_frame or master_half_by_frame.

verdicts.claim: ab_to_half exposes an unexplained ab abbreviation. The surrounding code uses A/B-style player identifiers, but the field does not name that concept as player IDs.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Rename it to player_to_half or player_id_to_half.

verdicts.claim: getpoint_ab combines an unexplained ab abbreviation with getpoint, leaving its role as the player credited with the point to be inferred from later winner logic.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Rename it to point_winner_player or point_winner_id.

verdicts.claim: Variable flipped suggests an action, but the logic detects inconsistent player sides rather than a flip event.
verdicts.verifier_note: The quote is present, but the claim is wrong: comparing one player's previous half with a later different half is exactly the detected side-flip state, so flipped is a clear boolean name.

verdicts.claim: The build_run_video_inputs docstring gives only a high-level purpose and does not orient a skimmer to its fixture-array loading and guard-input validation before assembling run_video arguments.
verdicts.quote: """Load one fixture and assemble its invariant ``run_video`` inputs."""
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add one sentence naming the fixture-array loads and guard-input validation.

verdicts.claim: RallyRow is a large positional record mixing ground-truth labels, predictions, eligibility flags and per-rally metrics, but has no docstring or field documentation.
verdicts.quote:
class RallyRow(NamedTuple):
    gt_index: int
    set_id: str
    rally: int
    n_gt_strokes: int
    classification: str
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add a class docstring describing the row and the ground-truth, prediction, eligibility and correctness field groups.
verdicts.verifier_note: The original docs-orientation claim says 23 fields, but the class has 27. The underlying schema-orientation concern remains. Original category: docs-orientation; correction: the field count.

verdicts.claim: ColumnAgg exposes primary and secondary correctness counts without stating that primary covers all ground-truth rallies while secondary covers detected rallies.
verdicts.quote:
class ColumnAgg(NamedTuple):
    primary_correct: int
    primary_total: int
    secondary_correct: int
    secondary_total: int
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add a class docstring defining primary as all-rally counts and secondary as covered-rally counts.
verdicts.verifier_note: Merged the docs-orientation and class-name findings for this record. The distinction is visible only by following score_video and flatten_metrics; one duplicate was folded in.

verdicts.claim: load_gt_tables has no docstring naming the four tuple positions. Its generic return annotation leaves the caller to infer master, homography, court-info mapping and resolution.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add a short docstring naming the four return positions.
verdicts.verifier_note: The original claim says there are no type hints, but a generic tuple return annotation is present. It does not identify the semantic role of each position. Original category: docs-orientation; correction: the type hint exists.

verdicts.claim: load_fixture_arrays returns an unnamed tuple of six NumPy arrays without documenting their order, shapes or dtypes.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add a short docstring naming the six return values in order and any non-obvious domain shapes or dtypes.

verdicts.claim: LandingFilterOptions is constructed with five positional numeric literals whose meanings are not explained at the call site.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Use named arguments when supported, or add named constants or a why-comment for the five values.

verdicts.claim: Reconciliation has no class docstring explaining its winner records, exact/deduplicated/mismatched frame counts, player-half flip counts and last-stroke offset.

class Reconciliation(NamedTuple):

    n_dedup: int
    n_mismatch: int
    n_ab_flip_rallies: int
    n_ab_flip_boundaries: int

verdicts.suggested_fix: Add a concise class docstring naming the frame-reconciliation counts, flip counts and offset.

verdicts.claim: DISPLAY_METRICS is a long tuple of metric keys with no explicit documentation of its output purpose or metric grouping.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add a short comment stating that the ordered keys drive the comparison table and captured reference literal.
verdicts.verifier_note: The name and its render_table and _literal consumers make the purpose partly inferable, so this is a modest orientation finding rather than an opaque-constant claim.

verdicts.claim: GtWinner does not clearly signal that the record contains ground-truth rally outcome data beyond the winner identity, including reasons, landing and player-half metadata.
verdicts.quote:
class GtWinner(NamedTuple):
    getpoint_ab: str | None
    winner_half: str | None
    win_reason: str | None
verdicts.suggested_fix: Consider a name such as GroundTruthRallyOutcome if the record exposes the full outcome.
verdicts.verifier_note: GtWinner is understandable and not misleading, but it is underspecified for a record carrying landing, reasons, mapping and flip metadata. This is a judgement-call unclear-name finding.
